design: cradle-to-gate LCA; primary data from two plants in one Italian municipality
comparison: metal-free synthetic-tannin tanning vs chrome tanning
method: 1 m2 finished leather; SimaPro 9.4; Ecoinvent; midpoint categories and single score
reported_result: metal-free route lower: particulate matter -25%, human toxicity non-carcinogenic -31%, carcinogenic -56%, acidification -29%; single score -18.4%; cattle breeding the largest contributor to several categories

design: LCA of one Italian artisan tannery; primary data
reported_result: substantial reductions for the vegetable route, ranging from 20% (ozone depletion potential) to 100% (human carcinogenic toxicity potential); chrome hotspot tanning/retanning; vegetable hotspot pickling, mainly liming

design: pilot-scale tanning of paiche (Arapaima gigas) skins
method: environmental performance indicators with grey clustering
reported_result: both chrome-free techniques classed better than chrome; best (phenolic) technique per 1000 kg skin: 30.0 m3 water, 2022.7 kWh energy, 105.5 kg solid waste, chromium not detectable in wastewater

comparison: triazine derivative + vegetable tannin vs chrome
reported_result: approximate values (g/L), chrome-free vs chrome: chloride 3.2 vs 11.3; TDS 8.5 vs 13.5; COD 13.2 vs 19.7; BOD5 4.6 vs 3.8; BOD5/COD 0.35 vs 0.19; the chrome-free process also omitted the NaCl pickle
BOD/COD ratio of the oxazolidine process reported as relatively lower than chrome tanning

design: laboratory tanning; burial and ISO 20136 test
comparison: zeolite-based tannage vs chrome and aluminium (burial)
reported_result: zeolite-tanned cow hide visibly more degraded than chrome- and aluminium-tanned hide after burial; ISO 20136 relative biodegradability vs collagen: 91.0% zeolite-tanned cow hide, 74.4% shoe-upper retannage, 0.5% chrome-tanned leather; zeolite leathers contained >12000 mg/kg aluminium

comparison: vegetable; oxazolidine; resorcinol-oxazolidine; Cr(III); Ti-Al; Ti-Zr
reported_result: all leathers biodegraded at different rates; oxazolidine- and vegetable-tanned more biodegradable than resorcinol-oxazolidine; abstract gives no single chrome vs chrome-free figure
vegetable-tanned leather produced more gas than chrome-tanned leather

comparison: wet-blue vs vegetable-tanned bovine leather and alternatives
reported_result: wet-blue fully degraded after 31-35 days; vegetable-tanned leather showed first degradation after 60 days and was not fully disintegrated at 90 days

comparison: hydrolysates of wet-white vs wet-blue leather as fertiliser
method: N release; soil indicators; Cr bioavailability
reported_result: both released 40-45% of total N in 42 days; DTPA-extractable Cr increased but stayed low in wet-blue-treated soil; Cr not bioavailable to tomato in either

design: field survey of 16 + 16 tanneries in Pakistan
comparison: chrome tanning cluster vs vegetable tanning cluster
method: metals in effluents and nearby soils
reported_result: Cr in soils near chrome tanneries well above background; near vegetable tanneries close to background

comparison: chrome (wet blue) vs seven chrome-free leathers
reported_result: Cr(VI) table entry <3.0 mg/kg; total Cr as reported in nominally chrome-free leathers up to 111.73 mg/kg (zeolite) and 53.72 mg/kg (aluminium); the same row gives the wet-blue leather 2.965 mg/kg, which looks internally inconsistent (possible unit error in the source)

design: in vitro comet assay (HepG2) on leather pieces
comparison: vegetable, synthetic and chrome-tanned bovine leather
method: alkaline comet assay after 24 h exposure
reported_result: all tanned leathers caused primary DNA damage vs untreated cells; highest after vegetable tanning, then synthetic, then chrome
